title: Brown Sugar Ham Steak with Scalloped Potatoes
subtitle: a thick ham steak seared with a brown sugar and orange glaze, beside creamy, golden baked scalloped potatoes
imageAlt: Glazed ham steak slices beside a scoop of creamy layered scalloped potatoes on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: The potatoes bake about 1 hour; the ham takes 8 minutes at the end.
Slice the potatoes 3 mm thin and even, by hand or on a mandoline with the guard.

steps.title: White sauce
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and butter a 20×20 cm (8 in) or 2 L baking dish. Melt the 3 tbsp butter in a medium pot over medium, whisk in the flour 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the milk. Add the garlic powder, dried thyme, salt and pepper and simmer 3–4 minutes, whisking, until it coats a spoon.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Layer a third of the potatoes and half the onion in the dish, then a third of the sauce. Repeat, then finish with the last potatoes and sauce, pressing down so the top is covered.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes. Uncover and bake 30–35 minutes more, until golden, bubbling and a knife slides through the potatoes easily.

steps.title: Glaze the ham
steps.text: With 10 minutes left, melt the 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium. Cook the ham 3 minutes a side until browned. Add the brown sugar and orange juice and turn the ham in the bubbling glaze 1–2 minutes, until sticky and 74°C (165°F) in the centre.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest the potatoes 10 minutes, then serve with the ham cut in pieces and the glaze spooned over.

fixIt.fix: Slices were too thick. Cover again and bake 15 minutes more.
The heat was too high; flour in the sauce usually prevents it. Bake at 190°C (375°F), not hotter.
Lower the heat as soon as the sugar goes in and keep the ham moving.

saleTip: Ham steaks are under $6 at No Frills and fully cooked, so dinner is fast; leftover ham goes into the split pea soup.
swap: Russet potatoes: they make a softer, starchier bake; same thickness and time.
leftovers: Diced ham and scalloped potatoes reheat together in one dish.
doneness: Ham steak is fully cooked; reheat to 74°C (165°F) in the centre (Health Canada, leftovers and reheated foods).
source: Based on tested scalloped potato methods (Canadian Living, Betty Crocker): thin-sliced potatoes layered with a thyme white sauce and onion, baked covered then uncovered at 190°C; ham steak pan-glazed with brown sugar.
gear: 20×20 cm (8 in) or 2 L baking dish
prepAhead: Bake the scalloped potatoes a day ahead; reheat covered at 180°C (350°F) for 25 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).
Mix the brown sugar and orange juice ahead.
reheat: Covered in the microwave 2–3 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Plain seared ham with scalloped potatoes; no glaze or dried thyme.

stepNotes.3: Basic: just sear the ham, no glaze.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: scatter the cheddar over the top when you take the foil off.

plating: A square of potatoes lifted out with a spatula.
Ham fanned beside it, glaze over.

why.0-3: A flour-thickened sauce keeps scalloped potatoes creamy and stops the milk from curdling.
why.0-0: Yukon Golds hold their slices and turn buttery.
why.1-3: Orange juice keeps the brown sugar glaze from tasting flat.

funFact: Scalloped potatoes have no scallops; the name likely comes from an old word for thin slices, 'collops'.

keeps.note: the potatoes go grainy when frozen
